page.text:
Differentiation investigates the first-order local linear approximation of
real functions.

Geometrically and conceptually, the derivative $f'(x_0)$ is far more than a
limit of secant slopes: it is the unique scalar such that:
$$ f(x_0 + h) = f(x_0) + f'(x_0) \cdot h + r(h), \quad \text{where} \quad \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{r(h)}{h} = 0. $$
The linear map $h \mapsto f'(x_0) \cdot h$ represents the tangent linear approximation
to $f$ at $x_0$, with an error $r(h) = o(h)$ that decays strictly faster than
the displacement $h$ itself. This formulation generalizes seamlessly to multivariable
Fréchet derivatives and forms the basis for the Chain Rule, Taylor expansions,
and the Mean Value Theorem.
